cn.name: Central North Zone
cn.bounds: North Zone (Central Flyway): east of the Continental Divide and north of I-40 and U.S. Hwy 54 at Tucumcari.
cn.note: Central Flyway. Ducks and coots Oct 10 – Jan 13. Dark geese Oct 17 – Jan 31. Light geese Oct 17 – Jan 31; Conservation Order Feb 1 – Mar 10.

cs.name: Central South Zone
cs.bounds: South Zone (Central Flyway): east of the Continental Divide and south of I-40 and U.S. Hwy 54 at Tucumcari (outside the Middle Rio Grande Valley).
cs.note: Central Flyway. Ducks and coots Oct 28 – Jan 31. Dark geese Oct 17 – Jan 31. Light geese Oct 17 – Jan 31; Conservation Order Feb 1 – Mar 10.

mrgv.name: Central South Zone — Middle Rio Grande Valley
mrgv.bounds: Valencia, Socorro and Sierra counties, in the Central Flyway South Zone.
mrgv.note: Central Flyway. Ducks and coots Oct 28 – Jan 31. Regular dark goose season closed; MRGV dark goose season Dec 19 – Jan 31 (2 a day, 2 a season). Bernardo and La Joya WMAs have set days.

pn.name: Pacific North Zone
pn.bounds: North Zone (Pacific Flyway): west of the Continental Divide and north of I-40.
pn.note: Pacific Flyway. Ducks Oct 19 – Jan 31 (scaup to Jan 12). Geese Sept 26 – Oct 11 and Nov 2 – Jan 31.

ps.name: Pacific South Zone
ps.bounds: South Zone (Pacific Flyway): west of the Continental Divide and south of I-40.
ps.note: Pacific Flyway. Ducks Oct 19 – Jan 31 (scaup to Jan 12). Geese Oct 17 – Jan 31.

seasonsNote: New Mexico is split between flyways at the Continental Divide: Central Flyway east (North, South and the Middle Rio Grande Valley), Pacific Flyway west (North, South). Each zone is tagged with its flyway.

seasons.label: Scaup
seasons.note: Central Flyway: scaup are open with ducks (1 a day).

seasons.label: Dark geese (Canada, cackling, white-fronted, brant)
seasons.note: Middle Rio Grande Valley: regular season closed; MRGV season Dec 19 – Jan 31, 2 a day and 2 a season.

seasons.label: Light geese (snow, Ross’s)
seasons.note: Central Flyway Light Goose Conservation Order Feb 1 – Mar 10 (free permit; electronic calls and unplugged shotguns; shooting to ½ hour after sunset except on WMAs).

seasons.label: Youth waterfowl days
seasons.note: 17 and under with an adult 18+. Central Flyway: ducks and coots only; Pacific Flyway: ducks, coots and gallinules.

bags.detail: Central Flyway 6 (no more than 5 mallards, 2 hens; 1 scaup; 3 wood ducks; 2 redheads; 2 hooded mergansers; 3 pintails; 2 canvasbacks). Pacific Flyway 7 (no more than 2 hen mallards, 2 redheads, 3 pintails, 2 canvasbacks, 2 scaup).
Central 1; Pacific 2. Inside the duck bag.
Central: 5 dark geese. Pacific: 5 Canada and brant plus 10 white-fronted (30 possession). MRGV: 2 a day, 2 a season.
Central 50 a day, no possession limit (Conservation Order: no limits). Pacific 20 (60).

duckSublimits.note: Central 5 (2 hens; Mexican ducks count as mallards); Pacific 2 hens

rules.d: One-half hour before sunrise to sunset; Bernardo, La Joya and other WMAs set their own hours and days (page 3–5).
Nontoxic shot for waterfowl, coots and gallinules; shotguns limited to 3 shells, except during the Light Goose Conservation Order.
Bernardo, La Joya and Jackson Lake have set days and species groups; Bernardo Ponds and Unit D open Mon, Wed and Sat during the Conservation Order. Not drawn.
East of the Continental Divide is the Central Flyway; west is the Pacific Flyway, with different dates and limits.

geometryNote: Geometry: the Continental Divide (USGS National Atlas), I-40 and US 54 (OpenStreetMap) and the Valencia, Socorro and Sierra county lines (Census TIGER), split against the Census TIGER outline and welded to Arizona, Utah, Texas and Oklahoma; State Game Commission lands; OpenStreetMap boat ramps; USGS NHD and GNIS; USFWS (refuge units; NWI marsh).
